business: KraftArt — a real tattoo & piercing studio in Masline, Podgorica (@tattoopodgorica), sold on portfolio + "book before you come", not on price or hype.
artDirection: A working atelier print job, not a website: paper-coloured ground (#efe9df), near-black ink, hard rules, one oxide red, and a monospace face used only for the labels a workshop actually writes down (address, artist handle, "Objava"). Nothing is rounded, nothing is shadowed, nothing floats — every surface is either paper, ink, or a photograph cropped hard by the container edge. The tone matches the trade: precise, unfussy, slightly clinical, and confident enough to lead with a finished forearm at full section height before making a single claim.
signatureElements: Container-cropped photography. The hero image (page.tsx:166-174) fills the 1fr column of a `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_0.8fr]` split and bleeds top-to-bottom of the section band — no padding, no frame, no radius. At 1440 it is exactly 640px wide and ~800px tall, cut by the section's own top and bottom ink rules. The photo IS the hero; the type sits beside it in the narrower column.

Two-tier rule system. `border-*-[var(--kraft-ink)]` (#090909) draws the structural cuts between major sections; `--kraft-line` (#cfc7b8) draws every hairline *inside* a section (hero CTA divider, step rows, contact rows). Same vocabulary, two weights, so the page reads as a ruled sheet with a clear hierarchy of division and never needs a card.

The mono label caste. IBM Plex Mono 400/500 at 0.7rem / uppercase / tracking-[0.14em] (the `label` constant, page.tsx:35-36) is reserved *exclusively* for metadata: nav, hero kicker, portfolio captions, artist strip label, address, phone numbers, contact values. It never sets prose and never sets a heading. That single rule is what makes the page read as an operating business rather than a template.

Portfolio caption plate + drawn hover. Under each frame: `@ziskatattoo` (mono, gray) left, `Objava` (mono, ink) right, baseline-aligned, then a 2px oxide bar that scales from `scaleX(0)` at the left origin on hover/focus (kraft.module.css:72-86). The hover state is a mark being drawn, not a card lifting.

Stencil wipe. Portfolio photos animate in with a `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0)` → `inset(0)` left-to-right wipe driven by `animation-timeline: view()` — CSS-only, no JS, no IntersectionObserver, double-gated behind `@supports` and `prefers-reduced-motion` (kraft.module.css:33-56). The motion is a metaphor for laying down a stencil, and it is applied to exactly two things.

The artist strip (page.tsx:248-269). A single-line, full-width band between two heavy sections: mono `Radove potpisuju` on the left, two 20px bold handles underlined in 2px oxide at 6px offset on the right. No bios, no headshots, no cards — the studio has no published biographies so the page prints none. It functions purely as a density break in the vertical rhythm.

Marker dash instead of numbering (page.tsx:291-294). Each `Prije termina` step is a three-column baseline row `sm:grid-cols-[3rem_1fr_1.4fr]`: a 40×4px oxide dash, the step title, then body at 1.4fr — hairline-separated. It gets the sequencing job done without the 01/02/03 idiom, and the dash survives the phone layout by re-anchoring to `col-start-1 row-start-1`.

CSS-drawn map plate. `MapEmbed` renders a graph-paper placeholder from two `repeating-linear-gradient`s in `currentColor` at 15% opacity — zero assets, palette-agnostic — behind a real button, so Google gets no request until the visitor asks. It is framed by `border p-1.5` (a mounted-plate inset) and the loaded iframe is `grayscale` so the map never out-colours the photographs.

Contrast-corrected accent twin. `--kraft-oxide: #8e302c` (6.7:1 on bone) plus `--kraft-oxide-bright: #d9564f` (5.1:1 on the near-black footer), with the measured ratios written into the CSS comments (kraft.module.css:15-21). One brand red that survives both grounds.

Named-destination mobile slab (page.tsx:407-438). An asymmetric two-cell `grid-cols-[0.9fr_1.1fr]` bar with a 2px ink top border, one cell inverted to ink, the other bone, each carrying a mono kicker (`Termin` / `Instagram`) over a bold destination name. No FAB, no radius, no shadow; body carries `pb-[calc(5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] md:pb-0` so nothing hides behind it.
typography: Two families, three roles, no serif anywhere. Archivo (grotesque, latin+latin-ext for č/ć/š/ž/đ) does display and body; IBM Plex Mono 400/500 does labels only. Display: `font-extrabold`, `leading-[0.92]`, `tracking-[-0.035em]`, `clamp(2.75rem, 9vw, 5.25rem)` on the H1 — the negative tracking at extrabold is what gives "Dođite da se crtamo." its cut-metal density. Section H2s are a fixed step down (`text-4xl sm:text-5xl`, `tracking-[-0.03em]`) and are identical across all five sections, so hierarchy comes from position and surrounding rules, not from ever-escalating size. Sub-heads: `text-2xl font-bold` (services), `text-xl font-bold` (steps, contact rows), all at `tracking-[-0.02em]`. Body is plain-weight Archivo, `leading-relaxed`, in `--kraft-gray`, hard-capped at `max-w-md` / `max-w-sm` / `max-w-2xl` per context so no measure ever runs long. Labels are the mono caste described above. There are exactly four type sizes above 16px on the whole page.
color: Five tokens scoped to `.page` in kraft.module.css:11-23. Grounds: `--kraft-bone` #efe9df (default) and `--kraft-paper` #e5ded1 (used for exactly one band — Usluge — bordered top and bottom in full-strength ink, so the section separates by paper stock rather than by a box). Ink #090909 sets type, all structural rules, and the inverted footer. Gray #635f59 carries every body paragraph and every mono label (documented at 5.2:1 on bone, 4.7:1 on paper). The oxide red appears in roughly eight places on the entire page and nowhere else: the "Art" in the wordmark, the hero kicker, the header CTA fill, the portfolio hover bar, the artist underlines, the step dashes, the contact-row hover, and (as the bright twin) the footer wordmark. Photographs supply all remaining colour — the blue wave and gold ear jewellery pop precisely because the page around them is two shades of paper.
composition: Hero (page.tsx:121-176): asymmetric `1fr / 0.8fr` split inside `max-w-6xl`; photo holds the wide column flush to the container's left edge and full section height, type holds the narrow one. The type column is `flex-col justify-between`, so the kicker/H1/subtitle sit at the top and the CTA pair + address are pinned to the bottom rail, baseline-matched to the photo's bottom crop, with a `--kraft-line` hairline above them.

Portfolio (page.tsx:180-224): section head is a `sm:flex-row items-end justify-between` pair — huge H2 left, mono 'Izbor sa zvaničnog profila · klik otvara objavu' right, both sitting on one full-width ink rule. The grid is a 12-column rail with a per-photo layout map (`WORK_LAYOUT`, page.tsx:51-72) keyed by image src rather than array index, so the rhythm is authored per photograph: row 1 = one 6-col 5:4 piece + two 3-col 4:5 thumbnails; row 2 = two 6-col squares. Variety comes from sizing, not from decoration.

Usluge (page.tsx:226-244): the only ground swap on the page. A `<dl>` in two columns, `gap-x-12 gap-y-10`, with no borders, no icons, no numbers — bold title, gray body at `max-w-sm`. The darker paper and the two ink rules above and below do all the containment work.
Artist strip (page.tsx:248-269): a deliberate density collapse — one 10-unit-tall band holding a mono label and two links. It exists to break the rhythm between two full sections.

Prije termina (page.tsx:274-305): title and intro run the full measure, then three baseline-aligned rows at `[3rem_1fr_1.4fr]` with `py-8` and hairline separators (first row explicitly skips its top border). Body copy is pushed into the wider right column so the titles form a clean scannable stack.

Kontakt (page.tsx:307-379): two columns, `lg:gap-16`. Left is a ruled list styled like a price board — bold label left, mono value right, `min-h-14`, hairline between rows, ink rule on top. Right is the map plate in a `border p-1.5` mount that matches the left column's height. Address closes the left column in mono.
Footer: full inversion to ink ground with bone type and the bright oxide twin, carrying the honest 'nezvanični dizajn koncept' disclosure — the tonal reversal ends the page rather than a CTA band.
interaction: Scroll-driven stencil wipe on portfolio photos via `animation-timeline: view()` with `animation-range: entry 10% entry 85%` — earns its place: it is the craft metaphor, it costs zero JS, and it is gated behind both `@supports` and `prefers-reduced-motion` with a static `clip-path: inset(0)` fallback.

`.slide` — 0.75rem translateY + opacity on service items and checklist rows, same view-timeline mechanism, `entry 20%–70%`. Borderline: this is the generic scroll-reveal the house standard warns about. It survives only because it is applied to two element types and never staggered per child.

Portfolio hover/focus: the oxide rule under the caption scales from `scaleX(0)` at left origin over 180ms. Earns its place — it is a drawn line on a page about drawn lines, and it replaces the banned hover-lift entirely.
Buttons invert on hover (ink → oxide for primary, outline → filled ink for secondary). Flat colour swap, no transform, no shadow. Earns its place.
Contact rows shift to oxide on hover, `min-h-14` targets. Earns its place — it is the only affordance signal a ruled list can carry.
Click-to-load map (`MapEmbed`): a real `<button>` gates the Google iframe, with a plain 'Otvori u Google Mapama' link as the zero-request fallback. Earns its place twice — privacy and LCP.

Focus: a single shared `focus-visible:outline-2 outline-offset-4 outline-[--kraft-oxide]` constant applied to every interactive element, including the sticky-bar cells (which use `outline-offset-[-5px]` so the ring stays inside the slab). Consistent and visible on both grounds.
Nothing loops, nothing parallaxes, nothing follows the cursor, no element fades in on the hero.
mobile: At 390px the page becomes a single ruled column and holds together on the rule system alone. The hero flips to photo-first (`h-60 min-[380px]:h-72`) then type, preserving the "evidence before claims" order; the CTA pair stacks full-width. The portfolio drops to one column and every frame normalises to `aspect-[4/5]` — the desktop's authored rhythm flattens into a consistent editorial scroll rather than trying to shrink a 12-column rail, and each photo keeps its mono caption line and hover rule. Services stack to one column with unchanged type sizes. The checklist re-grids to `[auto_1fr]` so the oxide dash stays on the title's line and the body wraps beneath it in column 2 — the marker never collapses to nothing. Contact rows keep label-left / value-right on one line at `min-h-14`, reading exactly like a printed price board. The fixed two-cell contact slab sits on a 2px ink border with `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` respected and matching body padding, and it names both destinations instead of hiding behind an icon. Every section keeps `px-5` and its full-bleed ink rule, so the vertical stack still parses as a sheet of ruled paper rather than a list of blocks.

transferableIdeas.idea: Two-weight rule system: one full-strength ink rule for structural section cuts, one hairline tint for divisions inside a section.
transferableIdeas.why: It replaces every card, every box, every shadow with a single consistent grammar, and it produces real hierarchy — you can tell at a glance whether a line separates two topics or two rows of the same topic. Nothing about it reads as generated.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Define two border tokens (`--x-ink`, `--x-line`). Use ink on `<section>` borders only; use the tint on every `border-t`/`border-b` inside a section. Ban `border-radius`, `box-shadow`, and background-filled cards from the page entirely. Works for a law firm, a bakery menu, a garage price list — anything with structured content.

transferableIdeas.idea: The mono label caste — reserve one monospace face exclusively for metadata and never let it touch prose or headings.
transferableIdeas.why: Uppercase mono at ~11px with wide tracking reads as something a business *records* (address, handle, order number, opening hours). Because it appears only where real facts appear, it makes the whole page feel like a document about an actual operation, not marketing copy.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Pick one mono, define one class (`0.7rem`, uppercase, `tracking-[0.14em]`, muted colour) and apply it to: nav, section eyebrow, image credits, address, phone, prices, hours, SKU/reference numbers. Enforce the rule that a heading never uses it. Swap the mono for a condensed grotesque or a small-caps face if mono is wrong for the trade — the discipline transfers, the face does not.

transferableIdeas.idea: Evidence before claim: open with one full-height, container-cropped photograph of finished work in the wider column of an asymmetric split, and let the pitch be a single sentence beside it.
transferableIdeas.why: It inverts the AI-hero default (badge + big claim + two pills + optional stock photo). The visitor sees what the business actually produces before being told anything, and the asymmetric column ratio plus a hard crop reads as art direction rather than a template slot.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: `grid-cols-[1fr_0.8fr]`, photo flush to the container edge and stretched to the section's full height with no padding or radius; type column `justify-between` so the CTA and the address pin to the photo's bottom crop. Substitute the photo for whatever the business's proof is — a dish, a finished kitchen, a rack of parts, a rendered plan.

transferableIdeas.idea: Per-item layout map keyed by content id, not by array index.
transferableIdeas.why: It lets you author a gallery's rhythm photograph by photograph (one wide 5:4 anchor, two narrow 4:5 thumbs, then a pair of squares) instead of dumping everything into a uniform grid — which is exactly the difference between a designed portfolio and a CMS dump.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: `const LAYOUT: Record<(typeof items)[number]["src"], {span: string; box: string}>` (page.tsx:51-72). Typing it as a `Record` over the literal union means TypeScript errors the moment someone adds or renames an item without giving it a layout. Reuse for any gallery, menu, project index, or case-study list.

transferableIdeas.idea: A one-line density-break band between two heavy sections.
transferableIdeas.why: Vertical rhythm needs a rest. A full-width strip holding one muted label and two large links costs 80px, breaks the section-section-section cadence, and gives real information a place to live that isn't another three-card grid.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: `flex sm:items-center sm:justify-between`, muted label left, one to three large bold links right. Use it for whatever short factual pair the business has: suppliers, certifications, the two people who do the work, the brands stocked, the two locations. Do not invent content to fill it — if there is nothing, drop the band.

transferableIdeas.idea: Separate one section by swapping the ground, not by boxing it.
transferableIdeas.why: A second, slightly darker tint of the same paper plus two full-strength rules isolates a section completely while keeping the page a single sheet. It is why the services block needs no cards, no icons and no dividers between items.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Add one ground token 4-6% darker than the base (`#efe9df` → `#e5ded1`), apply `border-y` in ink, and strip all interior chrome from the section's items — bold title, muted body, generous `gap-x`. Use it once per page, on the section that most wants to be read as a set.

transferableIdeas.idea: Contrast-corrected accent twin with ratios written into the stylesheet.
transferableIdeas.why: One accent almost never passes on both a light and a dark ground. Defining a second, brighter variant used only on the inverted surfaces means you keep a single brand colour visually while staying accessible — and documenting the measured ratio in a comment keeps the next developer from breaking it.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: `--accent` for light grounds, `--accent-bright` for dark ones, with `/* 6.7:1 on bone */`, `/* 5.1:1 on ink */` comments (kraft.module.css:15-21). Apply the bright twin in the footer and any inverted bar. Transfers to literally any palette.

transferableIdeas.idea: Motion chosen as a metaphor for the craft, implemented CSS-only with `animation-timeline: view()`.
transferableIdeas.why: A left-to-right clip-path wipe reads as a stencil being laid down — it means something on a tattoo page. It is scroll-linked (not a fire-once observer), costs no JavaScript, and is applied to exactly one element type, which is what separates it from scattered scroll-reveal slop.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Pick the verb the business physically performs and animate that: a wipe for a printer, a rise for a bakery, a slide for a joinery, an unfold for an architect. Implement as `animation-timeline: view()` inside `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` + `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, with the finished state as the static default. Limit it to one or two element types per page.

transferableIdeas.idea: Hover states that draw a mark instead of lifting a card.
transferableIdeas.why: A 2px accent rule scaling from `transform-origin: left` under a caption gives clear affordance feedback with zero layout impact and no shadow, and it visually belongs to a page built out of rules.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: `.item .bar { transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; }` + `.item:hover .bar, .item:focus-visible .bar { transform: scaleX(1); }`, transition gated behind `prefers-reduced-motion`. Always include `:focus-visible` so keyboard users get the same signal. Replaces `hover:-translate-y-1 hover:shadow-lg` everywhere.

transferableIdeas.idea: Let the absence of content be the design: document what the source did NOT publish, then ship no section for it.
transferableIdeas.why: The data.ts header (data.ts:1-14) records that the studio's public profile states no hours, no prices, no session lengths and no artist bios — so the page has no hours block, no pricing table, no team cards and no testimonials. Every remaining section is load-bearing. This is the single biggest reason the page does not read as generated: there is nothing on it that was invented to fill a layout.
transferableIdeas.howToTransfer: Before designing, write a source note at the top of the data file listing what is verified and what is unknown. Design only for the verified facts. When a section would need invented content — stats, testimonials, team bios, 'trusted by' — delete the section and let the page be shorter. Applies to every outreach demo regardless of trade.

weaknesses: Dead order utilities in the hero (page.tsx:166-174). `order-1 ... lg:order-2` is passed to `DemoPhoto`, whose `className` lands on the `` *inside* a `` — the grid item is the ``, which has no order at all. The rendered photo-left/text-right layout happens by default document order, not by the classes. Do not copy this pattern; put layout classes on the actual grid child, or the next person's attempt to reorder will silently do nothing.

Because of the above, the hero's `lg:border-r` on the type column renders as a vertical hairline at the container's *right* edge with nothing beyond it, while there is no rule at all between the photo and the type. The divider is on the wrong side of the split.

The desktop portfolio row 1 is ragged: `limun` at `lg:aspect-[5/4]` over 6 columns is roughly 110px taller than the two `aspect-[4/5]` 3-column thumbnails beside it, leaving a visible hole under `orah`/`katane` — which directly contradicts the comment at page.tsx:42-44 claiming no row trails off. Either match the heights or make the raggedness clearly deliberate; do not transfer the comment's confidence without transferring the fix.

The hero's right column at 1440 has roughly 300px of empty ground between the subtitle and the CTA hairline, produced by `justify-between` against an 800px photo. It reads as composure at this exact viewport but will keep growing on taller screens with no content to absorb it. Cap it (`max-h`, or move the rail into a nested block) before reusing.

Five of the source photographs carry the studio's own burned-in black watermark lozenge plus handle text, so the same black circle repeats five times down the gallery, colliding with the layout's own captions. The page cannot fix this, but do not adopt "let the client's Instagram watermark be the branding" as a technique — on a business with weaker source photos it would wreck the grid.

The gallery's variety comes almost entirely from cell sizing; three of the five works are near-identical forearm crops. With a flatter photo set the same `WORK_LAYOUT` technique would produce a monotonous wall. The technique needs shot variety to pay off — check the assets before committing to a rail-based gallery.

The `viber://` row in the contact list is a dead link for most desktop visitors (acknowledged in data.ts:27-28 and mitigated by printing the number, but the row still looks clickable and does nothing). If a scheme only works on one platform, either detect it or present it as text, not as a link row identical to the three live ones.

Mono at `0.7rem` with `tracking-[0.14em]` in `--kraft-gray` is right at the floor of comfortable reading — the desktop nav is effectively 11px. It passes contrast but not comfort. Bump the nav and the contact values a step if you reuse the label caste on an audience older than this one.

`.slide` (translateY + fade on services and checklist rows) is the one genuinely generic move on the page. It survives because it is unstaggered and used twice; copied more liberally it becomes exactly the scattered scroll-reveal the house standard bans.
